method.archive: ddev craft exec, read only: each person entry's serialized fields, office holdings related to it, entries related to it, and a Craft search of entries, assets and categories for each surname.
method.mirror: Python over every .htm, .html, .txt, .shtml, .asp, .php file and every flipbook search/bookText.xml under /Volumes/Reggie/SCVHistory/scvhistory.com (84,019 files), bytes decoded utf-8 or cp1252, case-insensitive regex per person (patterns in search_terms). names: Thomas M. Frew III (aka Thomas Frew Jr.)
persons.life_dates: January 31, 1895 to August 17, 1963 (Leon Worden, AP0724). Ruth Newhall (1996) gives birth year 1896.
persons.life_dates_note: Disagreement on the birth year: footnote both. Neither cites a document.
in_valley: Came to Newhall as a child in 1900 with his father, blacksmith Thomas McNaughton Frew II; served in World War I shoeing artillery horses; ran T.M. Frew & Son on Spruce Street (San Fernando Road), Newhall, after his father (Ruth Newhall 1996; Worden).
Converted the shop to a welding and machine shop, 1924 (City of Santa Clarita staff report, 2011).
Member, Newhall Chamber of Commerce from its founding, February 1923; Juvenile Welfare committee (Chamber minutes 1923).
A trustee of the American Legion theater corporation, 1940 (Bill Crowl, retrospective).
Newhall School District trustee for many years, several as president, retired by 1945 (roster note; Worden 1997, retrospective).
Among the sellers of the 23.86-acre Frew property added to William S. Hart Park, 1958 (County document).

in_valley: Came to Newhall January 1920; married schoolteacher Mattie Pearl Walk, Newhall Pass, June 20, 1920.
Ran the Ridge View (Ridgeview) Dairy with Pearl, 1920s to 1940s, at Highway 6 (Sierra Highway) and San Fernando Road (Newhall Avenue), the "Cook corner".
President of the Newhall-Saugus Kiwanis Club 1928 to 1935; Scoutmaster, Troop 2; World War I veteran, American Legion Post 507; Mason.
President of the Hart board when the Henry Mayo Newhall Auditorium was dedicated, September 12, 1952; gave the welcome and accepted the auditorium.
Died of a stroke at First Presbyterian Church, Newhall, May 9, 1954, while still a trustee. His widow Pearl later married fellow trustee Carleton Hadley (December 11, 1968).

persons.life_dates: January 29, 1906, Los Angeles, to 1979 (killed by a falling tree at Donner Lake) (Cassandra Skaggs, his granddaughter, 2017).
persons.life_dates_note: Retrospective family account; no death date to the day.
in_valley: Grew up from 1918 on his parents' 6-S Ranch, north of Soledad Canyon Road (today's North Oaks, Canyon Country).
With his brother Helm Jr. opened the 6-S Ranch Airpark in 1946 (Shell Progress, May 1947).
Drove a tanker truck for the Newhall oil refinery; after the ranch sold (1956) moved to Castaic and managed the hog farm at Wayside Honor Rancho (Skaggs).
Founding director of the Castaic Lake Water Agency, 1962 until his death in 1979; the agency's Earl Schmidt Filtration Plant on Lake Hughes Road is named for him.
Los Angeles County Sheriff's Auxiliary Force (Skaggs).
